lessons.title: DuckLake snapshots and time travel
lessons.summary: Every DuckLake commit is a snapshot recorded in a SQL catalog: read an older version, list what changed, and know what expiring snapshots removes.

blocks.title: Metadata in a database
blocks.body: DuckLake stores table data as Parquet files and all metadata (schemas, file lists, statistics, snapshots) in an ordinary SQL database: DuckDB, SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL. A commit is one database transaction, so several tables can change atomically, and finding a table's files is a query rather than a folder listing.

blocks.title: Snapshots and time travel
blocks.body: Every committed change creates a snapshot with an id and a time. SELECT * FROM lake.orders AT (VERSION => 2) reads the table as of snapshot 2, and AT (TIMESTAMP => ...) as of a moment. lake.snapshots() lists the snapshots, and lake.table_changes('orders', 2, 3) returns the rows inserted, deleted or updated between two of them.

blocks.title: Expiring snapshots
blocks.body: Old snapshots keep their Parquet files alive. Expiring them (ducklake_expire_snapshots) and then cleaning up old files frees the space, and time travel to an expired snapshot stops working. A schema change such as ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN is a snapshot too: older versions keep their old schema.

blocks.title: In the lab
blocks.body: Open the Lakehouse Lab: its DuckLake missions use the official ducklake extension on a local lake in the mission folder, and the checker reads snapshots and time travel with DuckDB. Then answer the concept checks below; they run nothing.

steps.title: A commit is a snapshot
steps.body: CREATE, INSERT and UPDATE each commit one transaction in the catalog database and add a snapshot.

steps.title: Read an older version
steps.body: AT (VERSION => n) reads the file list recorded for snapshot n: the Parquet files are still there. Take the ids from snapshots(); they depend on the lake's history.

steps.title: See what changed
steps.body: table_changes lists the rows inserted, deleted or updated between two snapshots: useful for incremental readers.

steps.title: Expire to free space
steps.body: Expiring old snapshots and cleaning up their files frees storage; those versions can no longer be read.
